title: Irregular verbs in the present
description: The everyday irregular verbs: ter, ir, fazer, poder, querer and more, plus têm and vêm, ter que and poder or querer with an infinitive.

guide.summary: The verbs you use most often are the irregular ones. Most are strange only in the eu form, many have a short one-syllable ele form, and ter and vir show their plural only with an accent. This page also covers ter que for have to and poder or querer with an infinitive.

sections.title: The eu form
sections.text: Most of these verbs are strange mainly in the eu form. Some swap a consonant (faço, digo, trago), some add one (vejo, venho, saio), and some are simply short words to learn by heart (sei, dou, vou, posso).
steps: Check whether the verb is on this list; if it is, do not build the eu form from the regular pattern.
Find its row and take the eu column.
Remember the families: z becomes ç or g (faço, digo, trago); ver and vir add a consonant (vejo, venho).

examples.pt: Eu faço o jantar e ele traz o vinho.
examples.en: I make dinner and he brings the wine.
I do not know the answer.

watch: Fazo, dizo and trazo do not exist.
Sei is the eu form of saber, but sabe and sabem keep the stem sab-.

sections.title: Short ele forms
sections.text: Many of these verbs have a one-syllable form for ele, ela and você, with no final vowel: tem, vai, faz, quer, diz, traz, vê, vem, dá, sai. The regular -e ending of -er verbs is simply missing.
steps: Ele, ela, você or one named person: look for the short form.
Do not add -e to faz, quer, diz or traz.
Keep the accent on vê and dá.
watch: Quere, faze, dize and traze are not Portuguese words.
Pode and sabe are regular-looking: they keep their -e.

sections.title: têm and vêm
sections.text: Ter and vir have the same sound in the singular and plural. Only a circumflex in writing shows the plural: ele tem, eles têm; ele vem, eles vêm. Ver is different: its plural doubles the e, with no accent since 2009.
steps: Is the subject plural (eles, elas, vocês, two people)?
For ter and vir, add the hat: têm, vêm.
For ver, write two e and no accent: veem.
watch: Teem and veem from vir do not exist.
The old spelling vêem is no longer used.

sections.title: ir and dar
sections.text: Ir and dar are irregular in every form, and they rhyme: vou / dou, vai / dá, vão / dão. The nós forms are vamos and damos.
steps: Find the subject's row.
Take ir for going, dar for giving.
Travel by vehicle: ir de ônibus, de carro.

examples.en: We are going to the beach.

examples.pt: Eu dou um presente para a minha mãe.
examples.en: I give my mother a gift.

watch: A gente vai means we go in casual Brazilian speech, but nós always takes vamos.
Imos and dam are not used.

sections.title: nós and the plural
sections.text: Outside the eu form, most of these verbs go back to the regular endings: nós fazemos, eles trazem, vocês sabem. Watch the few that stay odd: nós vimos from vir, nós saímos with an accent.
steps: Use the stem of the infinitive, not the stem of the eu form.
Add -emos or -em for -er verbs.
Learn vimos (vir), saímos (sair) and vamos, damos, vão, dão as they are.
watch: The ç of faço and the g of trago never spread: fazemos, trazem.
Vimos also means we saw, from ver; context tells you which.

sections.title: ter que + infinitive
sections.text: To say you have to do something, conjugate ter, then add que and the second verb in the infinitive. Ter de means the same and sounds a little more formal.
steps: Conjugate ter for the subject: tenho, tem, temos, têm.
Add que (or de).
Leave the second verb in the infinitive.
watch: Without que or de, ter does not mean have to.
Only ter changes: tenho que estudar, never tenho que estudo.

sections.title: poder and querer + infinitive
sections.text: Poder (can) and querer (want) are followed directly by an infinitive, with no word in between.
steps: Conjugate poder or querer for the subject.
Put the second verb straight after it, in the infinitive.

examples.pt: Ela quer sair hoje à noite.
examples.en: She wants to go out tonight.

watch: No de after poder or querer.
For a learnt skill, saber is more natural: Eu sei nadar.

steps: Find the verb's row in the table.
Take the eu form as written; do not build it from the regular pattern.
Check the subject is one person: ele, ela, você.
Use the short form with no added -e.
Decide whether the subject is plural.
Ter and vir: add the hat. Ver: write veem.
Find the subject's row.
Take the form of ir or dar written there.
Start from the infinitive's stem, not the eu form.
Add the regular ending, or use vimos, saímos as they are.
Conjugate ter.
Add que, then the infinitive.
Conjugate poder or querer.
Add the second verb in the infinitive, with nothing in between.

exercises.hint: The eu form does not keep the z of the stem.
exercises.feedback: Fazer changes its stem in the eu form only.
exercises.explanation: Eu faço: faz- becomes faç- before -o, with a cedilla to keep the s sound.

mistakes.why: That follows the regular pattern, but fazer is irregular in the eu form: the z changes to a different letter.
Faz is the ele / ela / você form. Eu has its own ending in -o.
Fazemos is the nós form, we. The subject here is only I.

exercises.hint: Like dizer and fazer, trazer changes its consonant in the eu form.
exercises.feedback: The eu form of trazer has a g.
exercises.explanation: Eu trago: the z of traz- becomes g, just as dizer gives digo.

mistakes.why: That is the regular pattern, which trazer does not follow in the eu form.
Traz is the ele / ela / você form, the short one. Eu ends in -o.
Traço belongs to another verb, traçar, to draw a line. Trazer takes a different consonant in the eu form.

exercises.hint: Dizer swaps its z for another consonant in the eu form.
exercises.feedback: The eu form of dizer is irregular.
exercises.explanation: Eu sempre digo a verdade: diz- becomes dig- before -o, like trago and faço.

mistakes.why: That is the regular pattern. Dizer changes its consonant in the eu form.
Diz is the ele / ela / você form. After eu the verb ends in -o.
Dizer is the infinitive. After a subject the verb has to be conjugated.

exercises.hint: Saber has a very short, irregular eu form.
exercises.feedback: Eu sei: the eu form of saber looks nothing like the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Eu não sei a resposta: sei is the eu form of saber, I know.

mistakes.why: That would be the regular pattern, but saber is irregular in the eu form.
Sabe is the ele / ela / você form. The subject is eu.
Saibo is not a Portuguese word. The eu form of saber is short and has no b at all.

exercises.instruction: Change ele to eu and adjust the verb.
exercises.source: Ele vê o mar da janela.
answers: Eu vejo o mar da janela.
exercises.hint: Ver has an irregular eu form with a j.
exercises.explanation: Eu vejo o mar da janela: the eu form of ver adds -j-.

answers: Eu vê o mar da janela.
mistakes.why: Vê is the ele form. Changing the subject means changing the verb too.

answers: Eu veo o mar da janela.
mistakes.why: That is not a form of ver. The eu form needs an extra consonant before -o.

answers: Eu vendo o mar da janela.
mistakes.why: Vendo is from vender, to sell. The eu form of ver is different.

alternatives.message: Right: estou trazendo says it is happening right now. Here, practise the simple present.

exercises.hint: Read I am bringing as a plan: Portuguese can use the simple present for that. Trazer is irregular in the eu form.
exercises.feedback: Use the eu form of trazer.
exercises.explanation: Eu trago o pão: trago is the eu form of trazer. For a plan like this the simple present is enough; for something happening right now, say estou trazendo.

mistakes.why: Trazer is irregular in the eu form; the regular -o ending on traz- is wrong.
Traz is the ele / ela / você form.

exercises.hint: The ele / ela form of querer is one syllable with no final vowel.
exercises.feedback: Querer drops its final -e in the ele form.
exercises.explanation: Ela quer: the ele / ela / você form is just quer.

mistakes.why: That adds the regular -e, but querer keeps the short form with no vowel at the end.
Quero is the eu form.
Querem is the plural form, for eles, elas and vocês.

exercises.source: Ela ____ um bolo para a festa.
exercises.hint: The ele / ela form of fazer is one short syllable.
exercises.explanation: Ela faz um bolo para a festa: the ele form of fazer ends in z with no vowel.

mistakes.why: The regular -e ending does not appear here; this verb uses a short one-syllable form.
Faço is the eu form.
Fazem is the plural form, for eles, elas and vocês.

exercises.hint: One person, one short syllable.
exercises.explanation: O João sempre diz a verdade: the ele form of dizer is diz.

mistakes.why: Digo is the eu form. The subject is João, one other person.
The regular -e ending is not used here; the form is shorter.
Dizem is plural, for eles, elas and vocês.

exercises.hint: Sair loses its r and keeps the stem sa- plus i.
exercises.explanation: Ela sai do trabalho cedo: the ele / ela form of sair is sai.

mistakes.why: Saio is the eu form.
Saem is the plural form, for eles, elas and vocês.
That is not a form of sair. The ele form ends in -i.

exercises.hint: The ele form of trazer is shorter.
exercises.explanation: Ele traz o vinho: the ele / ela / você form of trazer ends in z.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Trazer has a short ele form without a final vowel.
Trago is the eu form.
Trazem is plural; ele is one person.

exercises.hint: Ver has a one-syllable ele form with a hat accent.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is not a form of ver.
exercises.explanation: Ela vê a praia: vê is the ele / ela / você form of ver.

mistakes.why: Vee is not a word. The ele form of ver is one letter v plus e with an accent.
Vejo is the eu form.

exercises.hint: The ele form of querer is one syllable.
exercises.feedback: Use the short ele form of querer.
exercises.explanation: Ele quer um café: quer, with no final vowel.

mistakes.why: Querer does not take the regular -e in the ele form.
Quero is the eu form.

exercises.hint: Ele and eles sound the same here; only the accent shows plural.
exercises.explanation: Eles têm dois filhos: têm with a hat is plural; tem without it is singular.

mistakes.why: Tem without the hat is the singular form, for ele, ela and você. Eles needs the written plural mark.
Teem is not a word. The plural of tem keeps one e and adds an accent.
Tens is the tu form, rarely used in Brazil, and singular.

exercises.hint: Pais is plural. The plural of vem looks the same except for one mark.
exercises.feedback: Eles vêm: the hat marks the plural.
exercises.explanation: Os meus pais vêm amanhã: vêm, with a circumflex, is the plural of vem.

mistakes.why: Vem without the hat is singular, for one person. Pais is plural.
Veem belongs to ver, to see. Vir has a different plural.
Vimos is the nós form of vir, we come.

exercises.hint: The subject is plural. What mark does the verb need?
exercises.feedback: The plural tem takes a circumflex.
exercises.explanation: Elas têm muito dinheiro: elas needs têm, written with a hat.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Tem without the mark is singular, and elas is plural.
Teem is not a word. The plural of ter adds an accent, not a letter.
Tens is the tu form, singular.

exercises.instruction: Change ela to elas and adjust the verb.
exercises.hint: In speech nothing changes. In writing the verb gets a mark.
exercises.feedback: Tem becomes têm in the plural.
exercises.explanation: Elas têm um carro: the plural of tem is têm, with a circumflex.

mistakes.why: Tem without the hat stays singular. A plural subject needs the accented form.
Temem comes from temer, to fear.
Teem is not a word. Ter shows its plural with an accent.

exercises.hint: Ver doubles its e in the plural, and since 2009 it has no accent.
exercises.feedback: The plural of vê is veem.
exercises.explanation: Eles veem: two e, no accent in current spelling. Do not mix it up with vêm, from vir.

mistakes.why: Vêm is the plural of vir, to come. Ver writes its plural with two e.
That spelling was dropped in 2009. Today the plural of ver has no accent.
Vê is the singular form, for one person.
Vemos is the nós form.

exercises.hint: They is plural: the verb needs its written plural mark.
exercises.feedback: The plural of vem is vêm.
exercises.explanation: Eles vêm para casa cedo: vêm with a hat. Without it, vem is singular.

mistakes.why: Vem without the hat is singular, for one person. Eles is plural.
Veem is the plural of ver, to see.
Vêem is the old spelling of veem, from ver, to see. Vir puts the accent on a single e.

exercises.hint: Ir is completely irregular: its forms all start with v.
exercises.explanation: Nós vamos: ir has the forms vou, vai, vamos, vão.

mistakes.why: Imos is very old Portuguese and not used today.
Vão is the plural for eles, elas and vocês, not for we.
Vai is singular. In casual speech a gente vai means we go, but nós needs its own form.

exercises.hint: Dar rhymes with ir in the plural.
exercises.explanation: Eles dão: the plural of dar ends in -ão, just like vão.

mistakes.why: That is the regular -ar pattern, but dar is irregular here.
Dá is singular, for ele, ela and você.
Damos is the nós form.

exercises.hint: We: the form of ir that ends in -amos.
exercises.explanation: Nós vamos à praia no domingo: vamos is the nós form of ir.

mistakes.why: Vão is the plural for eles, elas and vocês.
Vai is singular. With a gente it is fine, but nós takes a different form.
Imos is not used in modern Portuguese.

exercises.hint: Eles: the plural form, which ends in -ão.
exercises.explanation: Eles vão ao cinema hoje: vão is the plural of ir.

mistakes.why: Vai is singular, for ele, ela and você.
Vamos is the nós form.
Iram is not a word. Ir uses forms starting with v.

exercises.source: I give a gift to my mother.
answers: Eu dou um presente para a minha mãe.
Eu dou um presente para minha mãe.
Dou um presente para a minha mãe.
Dou um presente para minha mãe.
exercises.hint: The eu form of dar ends in -ou, like vou.
exercises.explanation: Eu dou um presente para a minha mãe: dou is the eu form of dar.

answers: Eu dá um presente para a minha mãe.
mistakes.why: Dá is the ele / ela / você form. Eu ends in -ou.

answers: Eu dar um presente para a minha mãe.
mistakes.why: Dar is the infinitive; after eu the verb is conjugated.

exercises.hint: Você takes the same form as ele. Travel by a vehicle uses de.
exercises.feedback: Você vai: the ele / você form of ir.
exercises.explanation: Você vai de ônibus? Vai is the form for ele, ela and você. For several people, vocês vão.

mistakes.why: Vão is the plural form, for vocês. Você is one person.
No ônibus means on the bus, inside it. Going by a means of transport uses de.
Vou is the eu form.

exercises.hint: The nós form of vir is short and does not keep the e of vem.
exercises.explanation: Nós vimos: vir drops the -r and adds -mos to vi-. It looks like the past of ver, but here it means we come.

mistakes.why: Vemos is the nós form of ver, we see.
Virmos is the future subjunctive, a later topic.
Vêm is the plural for eles, elas and vocês.

exercises.hint: Only the eu form of saber is strange; the nós form is regular.
exercises.explanation: Nós sabemos: sab- + -emos, the regular -er ending.

mistakes.why: The odd stem sei- belongs to eu only. The other forms keep sab-.
Sabem is the plural for eles, elas and vocês.
Saber is an -er verb, so nós takes -emos.

exercises.hint: Vocês takes the eles form, regular here.
exercises.explanation: Vocês sabem falar inglês? Saber means to know how; vocês takes sabem.

mistakes.why: Sabe is singular, for one person.
Sabemos is the nós form, we.
Seiem is not a word. The plural keeps the stem sab-.

exercises.hint: Nós adds -imos, and the i takes an accent.
exercises.explanation: Nós saímos de casa às oito: sa- + -ímos. The accent splits the a and the i into two sounds.

mistakes.why: Sair is an -ir verb, so nós takes -imos, not the -er ending.
Saem is the plural for eles, elas and vocês.
Saio is the eu form.

exercises.instruction: Change eu to nós and adjust the verb.
exercises.hint: The ç belongs to eu only. Nós is regular.
exercises.explanation: Nós fazemos o jantar: faz- + -emos, the regular ending.

mistakes.why: The ç appears only in faço. The other forms keep the z.
Fazer is an -er verb: nós takes -emos.
Fazem is the plural for eles, elas and vocês.

exercises.hint: Trazer is an -er verb.
exercises.explanation: Eles trazem a comida: traz- + -em, the -er plural ending.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. -am is the -ar ending, and trazer is an -er verb.
The g belongs only to trago, the eu form.
Traz is singular.

exercises.source: We see our friends on the weekend.
answers: Nós vemos os nossos amigos no fim de semana.
Nós vemos nossos amigos no fim de semana.
Vemos os nossos amigos no fim de semana.
Vemos nossos amigos no fim de semana.
exercises.hint: Ver is regular in the nós form.
exercises.explanation: Nós vemos os nossos amigos no fim de semana: ve- + -mos.

answers: Nós vimos os nossos amigos no fim de semana.
mistakes.why: Vimos means we come (vir) or we saw (ver, in the past). The present of ver is different.

answers: Nós vejemos os nossos amigos no fim de semana.
mistakes.why: The j belongs to vejo only.

exercises.hint: Have to is ter que plus the infinitive. Put ter in the eu form.
exercises.explanation: Eu tenho que trabalhar amanhã: tenho, the eu form of ter, + que + infinitive.

mistakes.why: Tem is the ele / ela / você form.
Sou is from ser. An obligation uses ter que.
Estou is from estar. An obligation uses ter que.

exercises.hint: Ter needs a small word before the infinitive.
exercises.feedback: Ter que plus the infinitive: have to.
exercises.explanation: Você tem que estudar hoje. Ter de estudar means the same and is a bit more formal.

mistakes.why: Ter a is not used for have to.
Ter para estudar is not the obligation structure.
Ter em is not used before an infinitive.

exercises.hint: Ter que plus the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Nós temos que pagar: temos, the nós form of ter, + que + infinitive.

mistakes.why: Somos is from ser, to be. An obligation uses ter.
After que the second verb stays in the infinitive.

exercises.hint: Have to: ter que + infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Eu tenho que trabalhar amanhã. Tenho de trabalhar is also correct.

mistakes.why: Ter needs que or de before the infinitive to mean have to.
After que the verb stays in the infinitive.
Tem is the ele form.

exercises.source: Ele tem que estuda à noite.
answers: Ele tem que estudar à noite.
exercises.hint: Look at the verb after que.
exercises.feedback: After ter que, the verb is an infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Ele tem que estudar à noite: only ter is conjugated; the next verb keeps its -r.

answers: Ele tem que estuda à noite.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. After que the second verb does not take a person ending.
Without que, ter cannot mean have to.

exercises.instruction: Turn it into an obligation with ter que.
exercises.hint: Conjugate ter for eu, then que, then the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Eu tenho que dormir cedo: tenho que, then dormir in the infinitive.

mistakes.why: After que the verb goes back to the infinitive.
Tem is the ele form; eu needs its own form of ter.

exercises.hint: Você takes the ele form. The next verb stays as it is.
exercises.explanation: Você pode me ajudar? Pode is the você form of poder.

mistakes.why: Posso is the eu form: can I.
Podem is plural, for vocês.
Poda is not a form of poder in the present.

exercises.hint: The eu form ends in -o and keeps the stem quer-.
exercises.explanation: Eu quero comer agora: quero, then the infinitive.

mistakes.why: Quer is the ele / ela / você form.
Quis is the past, I wanted.
Queria is the imperfect, I would like, a polite variant but not the present.

exercises.hint: Can I: the eu form of poder, then the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Posso pagar? Posso is the eu form of poder.

mistakes.why: Pode pagar? asks whether you can pay, not whether I can.
After poder the second verb stays in the infinitive.

exercises.source: She wants to go out tonight.
answers: Ela quer sair hoje à noite.
exercises.hint: Querer + infinitive, with the short ele form.
exercises.explanation: Ela quer sair hoje à noite: quer, then sair in the infinitive.

answers: Ela quer sai hoje à noite.
mistakes.why: After querer the second verb stays in the infinitive.

answers: Ela quer de sair hoje à noite.
mistakes.why: Querer takes the infinitive directly, with no de.

answers: Ela quere sair hoje à noite.
mistakes.why: The ele form of querer has no final e.

exercises.hint: Look at the word between the two verbs.
exercises.explanation: Eu posso nadar bem: no word between poder and the infinitive. For a learnt skill, Eu sei nadar is even more natural.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Poder is followed directly by the infinitive.
After poder the second verb stays in the infinitive.

exercises.instruction: Add querer: they want to do it.
exercises.hint: Conjugate querer for eles, then put dormir in the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Eles querem dormir: querem, then dormir unchanged.

mistakes.why: After querer the second verb goes back to the infinitive.
Quer is singular.
